title: AI evaluation and governance
description: No change to a prompt or model reaches production until it passes a measured test and a recorded review. Production results flow back into the tests.

detail.role: Holds prompts, model choices, retrieval settings and guardrail rules as reviewed code.
detail.why: A prompt edit is a change to behaviour and gets the same discipline as code.

security.text: Every change needs a second reviewer, so no one can alter production behaviour alone.

detail.role: Runs the changed system over the test set and scores quality, safety, latency and cost per answer.
detail.why: A change is judged on measured results, not on a few spot checks.

cost.text: A 100-case smoke set runs on each change and the full 1,000-case set runs nightly, which keeps judge-model spend predictable.

risks.text: A smaller set is cheaper but can miss a regression that only shows on rare questions.

detail.role: Questions with reference answers, plus adversarial cases such as injection and data-leak attempts.
detail.why: The tests define what good means, so they are owned and reviewed too.

security.text: Known attack prompts are replayed on every release so old holes do not reopen.

risks.text: Real users ask things the set never imagined. Sampled production questions are added each month.

detail.role: Grades free-text answers against the reference and a rubric.
detail.why: People cannot read thousands of answers per release.

risks.text: A model grader favours long, confident answers. Its scores are calibrated against a sample that people also grade.

cost.text: Grading by model costs a small fraction of manual review, so it can run every time.

detail.role: Allows a release only when scores meet the thresholds and the required reviews are recorded.
detail.why: The rule is automatic and the same for everyone.

security.text: Any failed red-team case blocks the release, whatever the quality score.

risks.text: Too tight and nothing ships, too loose and regressions pass. Thresholds are owned by the platform team and change only by review.

detail.role: A named reviewer checks the use case's risk tier, data use and intended users before first release or a major change.
detail.why: Some questions need judgement: is this use of personal data acceptable?

security.text: Low-risk internal tools get a light check. Anything customer-facing or touching personal data gets the full review.

risks.text: Reviews add days to the first release. Later changes inside the approved tier skip this step.

detail.role: Records every model and use case in production: owner, version, risk tier, review date and intended use.
detail.why: You cannot govern what you cannot list.

security.text: The gateway refuses models that are not on the register.

risks.badge: Non-risk: shadow AI inside the platform
risks.text: Teams cannot call an unapproved model through the platform, since the register is enforced at the gateway.

detail.role: Serves users with the approved prompt, model and guardrails.
detail.why: What runs is exactly what was tested and signed off.

cost.text: A release that doubles tokens per answer shows up as a cost regression at the gate.

detail.role: Scores a sample of live answers, tracks refusals, guardrail hits, thumbs-down rates and spend, and alerts on drift.
detail.why: A model update or new kind of question can lower quality with no deployment at all.

security.text: A spike in blocked prompts often means someone is probing the system.

risks.text: A provider can change a hosted model without notice. Sampled scoring is how that is noticed.

links.label: Change opened
links.detail: A pull request starts an evaluation run on the changed prompt or configuration.

links.label: Test cases
links.detail: The pipeline reads the current cases for the use case's risk tier.

links.label: Grade answers
links.detail: Answers that need grading go to the judge model with the rubric, and scores come back.

links.label: Scores
links.detail: Quality, safety, latency and cost results are passed to the gate.

links.label: Needs sign-off
links.detail: If the change is new or moves the use case into a higher risk tier, the gate waits for the named reviewer.

links.label: Record release
links.detail: A passed release writes its version, scores and reviewer into the register.

links.label: Deploy
links.detail: Only a passed release is rolled out. The gate moves no user data.

links.label: Samples
links.detail: A sample of live requests and answers is streamed for scoring. Sensitive fields are redacted first.

links.label: New hard cases
links.detail: Poorly rated or flagged answers are reviewed by a person and added to the evaluation sets.
